title: Safeguarded Chain of Proof for Model-Related Incidents
author: Evelyn Park
content:
Summary

This playbook defines the controlled process for assembling, preserving, and delivering a safeguarded chain of proof (CoP) for incidents involving model serving, inference data, and tenant data residency concerns. It describes how RBAC signals, audit logs, model artifacts, network traces, and retention state are collected, correlated, and packaged for internal triage, legal hold, and regulator requests while preserving data residency constraints.

Scope

- Applies to incidents impacting model inference correctness, potential data exfiltration, privacy boundary violations, or suspected model-exfiltration vectors.
- Spans Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments where Redwood manages or coordinates evidence.
- Excludes low-severity telemetry anomalies that are resolved by automated regressions (see "Related low-severity flow" below).

Definitions

- Chain of Proof (CoP): Ordered, cryptographically timestamped artifacts that together demonstrate what happened, when, and who/what acted.
- Evidence Package (EP): Compressed archive (.tar.gz) containing logs, manifests, signed digests, and a custody ledger.
- Custody Ledger: JSON manifest recording handlers, transformations, and storage locations with ISO8601 timestamps and signatures.

Roles and responsibilities

- Security Incident Lead (SIL) — Security: declares legal hold, directs collection priority, approves export.
- Oncall SRE (SRE): captures infra telemetry, network PCAP (if authorized), and CPU/GPU scheduling traces.
- Model Owner (ML Eng): exports model artifact version, weights checksum, inference cache dump, and prompt seeds used during triage.
- Compliance/Legal: declares regulatory constraints and export approvals (e.g., cross-border restrictions).
- Customer Success (if customer-facing): coordinates customer notifications per contract/SLA.

Evidence capture flows (high level)

1) Triage and scope capture (first 30 minutes)
   1. Declare incident in PagerDuty -> Incident channel created.
   2. SIL posts evidence priority (must-collect / optional) and legal hold indicator.
   3. SRE runs automated collection script: redwood-collect init --incident $INC_ID --level triage

2) Live artifact stabilization (0-4 hours)
   1. Freeze routing rules for affected models (runtime command): rctl route freeze --model MODEL_ID --reason "evidence-capture"
   2. Snapshot relevant runtime KV cache to ephemeral storage: rruntime snapshot --model MODEL_ID --out /tmp/${INC_ID}_kv.snap
   3. Export audit-log window (example BigQuery/GCP query):
      bq query --format=json '\n        SELECT * FROM `redwood-prod.audit_logs`\n        WHERE timestamp BETWEEN "2026-08-15T10:03:00Z" AND "2026-08-15T10:33:00Z"\n      ' > /evidence/${INC_ID}/audit.json

3) Model & prompt evidence (0-8 hours)
   - Owner exports: model manifest (model-manifest.yaml), model weights checksum (sha256), and the pinned model image tag. Example manifest snippet:

     model: 
       id: MODEL_ID
       version: v2026-06-12
       registry: ghcr.io/redwood/models
       digest: sha256:abc123...

   - Prompt seeds: collect canonical prompts used for repro (redwood-eval export --seed-set incident-REPR_SEEDS). Prompt content may be redacted if it includes PII; see Redaction rules below.

4) RBAC & entitlement evidence (0-2 hours after SIL directive)
   - Capture role bindings snapshot (RBAC export):

     curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n       https://auth.redwood.internal/v1/entitlements/snapshot?at=2026-08-15T10:05:00Z \\n       > /evidence/${INC_ID}/rbac-snapshot.json

   - Gather just-in-time elevation tokens and JIT activation logs (if used).

5) Data residency & retention state (legal hold step)
   - Query retention index for affected tenant(s): retentionctl query --tenant TENANT_ID --interval "2026-08-01/2026-08-15" --format json \n     > /evidence/${INC_ID}/retention-state.json
   - If the tenant is geo-fenced, mark EP as region-restricted and follow export approval (Compliance signature required).

Packaging the Evidence Package (EP)

- Minimal EP contents (required):
  - custody-ledger.json (see example below)
  - audit.json (audit-stream slice)
  - rbac-snapshot.json
  - model-manifest.yaml and model-digest.txt
  - network-traces/* (if authorized)
  - hashes.txt (sha256 sums for every file)

- Example custody-ledger.json (must be produced exactly in this schema):

  {\n    "incident_id": "INC-2026-1234",\n    "collected_by": "oncall-sre@example.internal",\n    "collected_at": "2026-08-15T10:42:12Z",\n    "items": ["audit.json","rbac-snapshot.json","model-manifest.yaml"],\n    "signature": "SIGNATURE_PLACEHOLDER"\n  }

- Create package and sign (recommended process):

  tar czf ${INC_ID}-evidence.tar.gz -C /evidence ${INC_ID} && \\n  cosign sign --key ksm://projects/redwood/keys/evidence-signing ${INC_ID}-evidence.tar.gz

Preservation storage and retention policy

The EP lifecycle is controlled by the legal hold state and the retention matrix below. Storage locations are encrypted at rest and tagged with incident metadata.

Retention matrix (text table)

- For display, this table shows the artifact class, default retention, and cross-border export allowance.

| Artifact class | Default retention | Cross-border export allowed? | Storage class | Owner |
|---------------|------------------:|-----------------------------|---------------|-------|
| Audit slices   | 3 years           | No (requires Compliance OK)  | encrypted S3  | SRE   |
| RBAC snapshots | 2 years           | No (internal only)           | encrypted S3  | Security |
| Model manifests| 5 years           | Yes (if model-only)          | registry (immutable) | ML Eng |
| Network traces | 6 months          | No (sensitive)               | secure vault   | SRE   |
| Prompt seeds   | 1 year (redacted allowed) | No (PII must be redacted) | secure vault | ML Eng |

Note: storage classes map to internal buckets: s3://evidence-prod, s3://evidence-region-RESTRICTED, registry://models/immutable.

Cross-border export and approvals

- Any EP containing tenant data with residency constraints requires an Authorization to Export token from Compliance and an explicit Compliance signature on the custody ledger. Approval flow: SIL -> Compliance -> Legal -> exec sign-off (for regulator requests). Approval must be logged in the custody-ledger under approvals[].

Handling PII and redaction rules

- If prompts or logs contain PII, the Model Owner or SIL must create a redacted copy where:
  - Replace overt identifiers with stable pseudonyms (pseudo-USER-1234).
  - Keep indices to allow cryptographic linkage to raw material without exposing PII.
- Redaction manifest must include algorithm used, salt, and who performed redaction. Example redaction entry in custody-ledger: "redaction": {"performed_by":"ml-eng@example.internal","method":"sha256-salt-v1","salt_id":"ksm://redwood/salts/01"}.

Evidence access control and RBAC enforcement

- EPs are stored in s3://evidence-prod/<INC_ID>/ and ability to download is gated by a short-lived presigned URL service. Presign policy: max TTL 24 hours except for Legal, who can request 7-day presigned URLs via ticketing and two-person review.

- Access roles required: security.incident_viewer, security.incident_admin, legal.export_approver. All access is logged to the audit stream and mirrored into the immutable audit store.

Chain of custody integrity checks

1. Verify SHA256 hashes in hashes.txt against files in EP.
2. Verify cosign signature against the company evidence signing key.
3. Verify custody-ledger signatures are present (cosigned by collector and by SIL).

Automated evidence sanity checks (CI for incidents)

- redwood-collect validates: presence of required artifacts, manifest consistency, and a simple schema check. Failures produce a content-report.json that must be resolved before signing.

Release control and rollbacks

- If model rollback is part of remediation, approval must be recorded in custody-ledger with the rollback command exactly as executed. Example rollback command recorded: 

  rctl model promote --from-tag v2026-06-12 --to-stable --reason "incident rollback INC-2026-1234"

Regulatory disclosure & packaging for auditors

- For regulator requests the EP must include: custody-ledger (signed), redaction manifest (if used), export-approval record (Compliance signature), and a short narrative (one-page) signed by SIL summarizing scope, timeline, and affected tenants.

Incident closure and retention transitions

1. SIL closes incident and sets legal_hold: true/false in custody-ledger.
2. If legal_hold == true, retention transitions to "indefinite until release" and Compliance must maintain a release ticket.
3. If legal_hold == false, lifecycle moves to archival per retention matrix above.

Audit & review cadence

- Security-run quarterly tabletop exercises will validate the evidence capture path end-to-end. Each exercise produces a compliance report stored under s3://compliance-exercises/<year> with postmortem and a list of improvements.

Appendix A — Example commands and snippets

- Export a time-window of auth decisions from the decision-store (example):

  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n    'https://auth.redwood.internal/decisions?tenant=TENANT_ID&from=2026-08-15T10:00:00Z&to=2026-08-15T11:00:00Z' \\n    | jq . > /evidence/${INC_ID}/decisions.json

- Create a signed evidence package (example):

  cd /evidence && tar czf ${INC_ID}-evidence.tar.gz ${INC_ID} && \\n  cosign sign --key ksm://projects/redwood/keys/evidence-signing ${INC_ID}-evidence.tar.gz && \\n  sha256sum ${INC_ID}-evidence.tar.gz > ${INC_ID}-evidence.sha256

Appendix B — Quick checklist (for SIL at time of declaration)

- [ ] Declare incident and create incident channel
- [ ] Issue legal hold if tenant data is involved
- [ ] Run redwood-collect init --incident $INC_ID
- [ ] Request RBAC snapshot and decisions export
- [ ] Ensure model owner exports model-manifest and prompt seeds
- [ ] Approve EP packaging and signature
